claim.pdf_says: 14.9.14.4  General rules  — a fourth-level clause heading, one level below 14.9.14 EXIT statement, identical in rank to 14.9.15.4, 14.9.16.4 and 14.9.17.4.
claim.markdown_says: ## 14.9.14.4 General rules   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27107 — level 2, the same level as '## 14.9.14 EXIT statement' at line 27013, whereas '### 14.9.15.4 General rules' at line 27170 is level 3)
claim.why_it_matters: The heading is promoted a level, so General rules for the EXIT statement renders as a sibling of the EXIT statement clause itself instead of a child. That breaks the generated outline/TOC nesting and any tooling that walks the markdown heading tree to map clause numbers to sections.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against the 300-dpi render of PDF page 655 (printed folio 625) and against specs/ISO_COBOL.md. PDF: the page prints, in bold run-in style, '14.9.14.4 General rules', immediately after syntax rule 10 ('The EXIT statement with the PARAGRAPH phrase may be specified only in a paragraph.') and immediately before 'FORMAT 1' / general rule 1. The four-component clause number 14.9.14.4 is by ISO numbering one level below the three-component 14.9.14 EXIT statement. Note the PDF's own typography does NOT distinguish these depths: on page 653 '14.9.14 EXIT statement', '14.9.14.1 General' and '14.9.14.2 General formats' are all set in the same bold face and size, so rank is carried by the clause NUMBER alone, not by font. MARKDOWN: line 27110 reads '## 14.9.14.4 General rules' (level 2), preceded at 27109 by the correct anchor ''. '## 14.9.14 EXIT statement' is at line 27016, also level 2 — so the subclause is a sibling of its own parent. The transcription is inconsistent with ITSELF, which is decisive: within the very same clause, 14.9.14.1 (27019) and 14.9.14.2 (27032) are '###' while 14.9.14.3 (27061) and 14.9.14.4 (27110) are '##'; and the adjacent clauses 14.9.15.4 (27173), 14.9.16.4 (27220) and 14.9.17.4 (27307) are all '###'. Doc-wide, four-component headings are 620x '###' vs 162x '##' vs 24x '####', so '###' is unambiguously the intended convention and this instance is a defect. Attempts to refute failed: the heading is not missing, misplaced or reflowed — it is present with verbatim-correct text; it is not page-break furniture (it sits mid-page, not at a page boundary); and it is not mere cosmetic formatting, because markdown heading depth IS the document tree that outline/TOC generators and clause-mapping tooling walk. The claim therefore survives, with corrections below.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, but mislabeled and misquoted on details; also under-scoped. (1) Nothing is missing — kind 'missing-heading' is a misnomer. The heading text '14.9.14.4 General rules' is present and verbatim correct, and its anchor '' is present and correct. The defect is heading DEPTH only: '##' where the file's own convention and the ISO clause numbering both require '###'. Correct kind is 'heading-level' / 'wrong-heading-depth'. (2) All three cited line numbers are off by 3. Actual: '## 14.9.14.4 General rules' is line 27110 (not 27107); '## 14.9.14 EXIT statement' is line 27016 (not 27013); '### 14.9.15.4 General rules' is line 27173 (not 27170). (3) The claim treats this as an isolated instance; it is not. Its immediate sibling '## 14.9.14.3 Syntax rules' (line 27061, PDF page 654) has the identical defect, as does '## 14.9.13.3 Syntax rules' (26868), '## 14.9.13.4 General rules' (26939) and '## 14.9.18.4 General rules' (27392). Doc-wide there are 162 four-component headings emitted at level 2 against 620 correctly at level 3 — a systemic OCR/transcription class that should be fixed by a single sweep normalizing heading depth to the component count of the clause number, not by a one-off edit to page 655. (4) Severity should be tempered: no normative CONTENT, wording or COBOL semantics is affected, and cross-references that resolve by clause number or by the section-14-9-14-4 anchor still work. The breakage is limited to consumers that infer hierarchy from '#' depth.
